clue.text: Sounds like cattle going round about dead depraved city

indicators.note: about means the turned word wraps around the letter for dead
going round turns the cattle's sounds back to front

parts.note: the sounds cattle make are moos

explanation.surface: A lowing herd ambles round a corpse in a wicked town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' looks like a homophone signal but simply leads to the noises cattle make, MOOS; 'going round' turns that to SOOM, and 'about' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed for its wickedness is the byword for a place of vice.

clue.text: Australian icon rehabilitating latest prisoners

indicators.note: rehabilitating, restoring to a new state, signals the letters of latest prisoners are reshaped

explanation.surface: A national treasure helps reform the newest inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Les Patterson is the boorish Australian cultural attaché created by comedian Barry Humphries.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous comic character of Barry Humphries is an example of a national icon of Australia.

clue.text: Scottish clan mostly morose over more than half of local city

indicators.note: over places the first part above the second in this down entry
mostly says the word for morose loses its final letter

parts.note: dour means stern and morose

indicators.note: more than half of keeps four of the seven letters of the city

parts.note: Glasgow is the city local to a Scottish clan

explanation.surface: A clan described as largely gloomy, sitting over a portion of a nearby city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims DOUR to DOU; 'more than half of' cuts GLASGOW to GLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Douglases are a powerful Lowland family, an example of a Scottish clan.

clue.text: Knowledgeable literary girl is embraced by graduate, that is

indicators.note: embraced by puts the word is between the graduate and that is letters

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A clever girl from fiction is hugged by a graduate, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry James wrote the novel What Maisie Knew, hence 'Knowledgeable'.
explanation.definitionFit: The child heroine of Henry James's novel is famous for what she knew, an allusive definition.

clue.text: A little interest in science completely reversed

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for interest inside the one for science

parts.note: INT is the usual abbreviation for interest in finance

indicators.note: reversed says the word for completely is written backwards

parts.note: completely means all

explanation.surface: A scientist admits barely any enthusiasm, and that grudgingly turned on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny trace or spark of something is a synonym for a very small amount.

clue.text: Consequence of burning in abandoning vessel in difficulty?

indicators.note: abandoning means the word in is left out of the troubled vessel

parts.note: a sinking raft is a vessel in trouble
taken as written

explanation.surface: Abandoning ship in a fire is a desperate measure with painful aftermath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' removes IN from SINKING RAFT, leaving S KING RAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe burns are often treated by transplanting healthy tissue, so the procedure follows burning.

clue.text: River Test eradicated in hard work

indicators.note: eradicated in says the word for test is wiped out of the word for hard work

parts.note: industry means diligent hard work
try means test

explanation.surface: The River Test, a Hampshire trout stream, is wiped out by heavy industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' looks like the English river; here it means TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: The great river of Pakistan, which gave India its name, is an example of a river.

clue.text: Stomach set to be upset — eat worriedly after some hesitation

indicators.note: after places the rearranged eat following the hesitation
to be upset, in a down entry, means turned upside down so read backwards

parts.note: a lot is a set of items, as at an auction
er is a sound of hesitation

indicators.note: worriedly signals the letters of eat are disturbed

explanation.surface: An anxious eater hesitates over a stomach-churning meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be upset' turns LOT into TOL; 'worriedly' rearranges EAT into ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up with something is the verb sense, as in being unable to bear a person.

clue.text: Mild drink (seconds repeatedly declined) then start on fag

indicators.note: declined means those letters are turned down and dropped

parts.note: slight means mild or minor
sup means to drink

indicators.note: repeatedly says the seconds letter is wanted twice over

explanation.surface: Someone turns down second helpings of a light beer, then reaches for a cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declined' drops both S's from SLIGHT SUP. 'Fag' is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignite a cigarette is to begin smoking it, the phrasal verb used for lighting up.

clue.text: Water supplier de-ices marsh fluidly with gang in support

indicators.note: in support places the gang underneath, holding up the rest in this down entry
fluidly suggests the letters of de-ices marsh flow into a new order

parts.note: a crew is a gang

explanation.surface: A water pump that thaws a frozen bog, backed up by a work gang.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient helical pump lifts water for irrigation, supplying it from a lower level.

clue.text: Unusually fired about English set of colleges brought back together

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other pieces
unusually signals the letters of fired being set in an uncommon order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram
a university, informally UNI, is a set of colleges

explanation.surface: Staff unexpectedly sacked at an English university are later reinstated together.
explanation.definitionFit: To reunite something split apart, as Germany was in 1990, is to make it one again.

clue.text: Reason name is dropped from extended current course at first

indicators.note: is dropped from removes the letter for name out of the word for extended

parts.note: something extended is long
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of course

explanation.surface: An instruction about trimming a long electrical course reads like technical small print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is dropped from' takes N out of LONG, leaving LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound reasoning or rational argument is what logic means; the noun reason is a close synonym.

clue.text: Queen's preference excluding one feature of Schubert song

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the 's simply attaching what follows

indicators.note: excluding means a letter is left out of the word for preference

parts.note: a liking is a preference
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: The monarch's taste apparently leaves out a highlight of a Schubert lied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding' takes I out of LIKING, leaving LKING. Schubert set Goethe's poem Erlkönig, whose sinister title figure lures a child to death.
explanation.definitionFit: The elf-king of Goethe's ballad is the central character of Schubert's famous song, so a feature of it.

clue.text: Recalled laughs with a tenor getting out of place in fugal passages

indicators.note: getting out of place says the tenor letter shifts to another spot
recalled, as in called back, means the word for laughs is reversed

parts.note: titters are nervous little laughs
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: Remembered giggling with a tenor who was out of position in a fugue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns TITTERS into SRETTIT; 'getting out of place' moves its final T up to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fugue the stretto, plural stretti, is a section where entries overlap closely.

clue.text: He will avoid embraces or other amorous activity

indicators.note: will avoid says the letters of he are kept out of the word for embraces

parts.note: pashes is slang for passionate embraces or crushes
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of a shy man who steers clear of cuddles and all romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like the subject of the sentence, but its letters are what 'will avoid' removes. PASH is chiefly British and Australian slang for a snog or a crush.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a flirtatious advance at someone is the informal sense, as in making a move on them.

clue.text: Town pub — new thing everyone relies on?

parts.note: a bar is a pub
a staple is a basic item everyone depends on

explanation.surface: A local pub has become an essential new fixture for the whole town.
explanation.walkthrough: BARNSTAPLE is a market town in north Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Devon market town is an example of a town, the bare definition.

clue.text: Poverty? Observed rises when bringing in feeds

indicators.note: when bringing in means the reversed word takes the word for feeds inside it
rises, in a down entry, means the word reads upwards so backwards

parts.note: observed means seen
dines means feeds

explanation.surface: Visible hardship increases as more people need feeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' signals reversal because this is a down entry, read from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Want or destitution is the state of being in need, a near synonym marked by the question mark.

clue.text: Copper vehicles having centre removed in workspaces

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: having centre removed takes out the two middle letters of the vehicles

parts.note: bicycles are vehicles

explanation.surface: A police officer's bikes are gutted in the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman but gives CU; 'having centre removed' takes YC out of BICYCLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Small partitioned booths in an open-plan office are spaces where people work.

clue.text: Unable to say one note's overlooked by one duetting badly

indicators.note: overlooked says one letter for note is left out of the pool
badly signals the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram pool

explanation.surface: A singer is speechless because one duet partner ignored a note and sang poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlooked' drops an N from ONE DUETTING, and 'badly' shuffles the other ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being speechless from shyness or nerves is the idiom; the phrase pictures a tongue bound in place.

clue.text: River and sea not ruffled by this wind

indicators.note: ruffled, as water is by wind, signals the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A wind so gentle that neither river nor sea is disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale from between north and east is a compass wind, the dialect form used by sailors.

clue.text: Man retains work in aspiration

indicators.note: retains means the pronoun keeps the word for work inside it

parts.note: he, the masculine pronoun, stands for a man
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A man holding on to his job is full of ambition.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiration is a wish or ambition for the future, a close synonym.

clue.text: Plea to songwriter not found in the building?

definitions.meaning: split as ..., it is an appeal to a composer to write a tune

explanation.surface: A songwriter is begged for an outdoor concert number.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits into three words: O, an appeal, PEN, write, and AIR, a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taking place outdoors rather than inside a building is out in the fresh atmosphere.

clue.text: Say overture of Mozart's not mistaken for overture of Beethoven

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

indicators.note: overture of here means the opening letter of the next word
mistaken signals the letters of not are rearranged

explanation.surface: A concert-goer wrongly takes Mozart's opening piece for Beethoven's.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'overture of' means only a first letter, M; the second is a real overture.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven wrote incidental music for Goethe's play, and its overture is his famous concert piece.

clue.text: Wrong about a piece of jewellery

indicators.note: about means the word for wrong goes round the letter A

parts.note: erring means being in the wrong

explanation.surface: Someone is mistaken about a particular item of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament worn on the lobe of the ear is an example of jewellery.

clue.text: English writer goes crazy about son

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters surround the letter for son
crazy signals the letters of goes are jumbled

explanation.surface: An English author loses his mind over his boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges GOES as GOSE, and S goes inside. Edmund Gosse wrote the memoir Father and Son, which suits 'about son'.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Gosse, Victorian critic and memoirist, is an example of an English man of letters.

clue.text: One company excluded from US politicians gets access

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: excluded from takes the company letters out of the word for US politicians

parts.note: Congress is the US legislature, a body of politicians

explanation.surface: A lone firm shut out of Washington lobbying still finds a way in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluded from' takes CO out of CONGRESS, leaving NGRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The act or right of entering a place is a formal synonym for entry or admission.

clue.text: Unambitious section with shops

parts.note: a mall is a collection of shops

explanation.surface: A modest department in a shopping centre, lacking any grand plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Small-minded or modest in scale describes plans or people lacking big aims.

clue.text: Sure goats can be mistaken for a reptile?

indicators.note: can be mistaken suggests the letters of sure goats taken in a wrong order

explanation.surface: Seeing certain goats in poor light, someone confuses them for a lizard.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a dinosaur is only loosely a reptile.
explanation.definitionFit: The plated Jurassic dinosaur is an example of an ancient reptile, hence the question mark.

clue.text: All one has: cup from Paris caught in fishing tackle

indicators.note: caught in means the French word sits inside the fishing tackle

parts.note: nets are tackle used for fishing
tasse is French for cup

explanation.surface: A trawlerman's entire wealth amounts to a French cup tangled in his nets.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounting, what remains after liabilities are subtracted is the total worth of everything owned.

clue.text: Sound of painful attack — wrestling manoeuvre?

indicators.note: sound of means the word for painful attack is said aloud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: a throe is a violent spasm of pain

explanation.surface: The noise of a painful onslaught during a wrestling bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurling an opponent to the mat is a basic move in wrestling and judo.
